tasks.task: Write a requirements document with a test for every line

items.when: When a client brings an idea, a sketch or a handmade sample and wants a factory order
When each requirement needs a measurable target, a test method and an owner
When a requirement says 'durable' or 'light' and needs a number and a finish line
When the document is drafted, to have reviewers hunt for hidden assumptions and failure points
When the list keeps growing and you must ask which features the product can do without

tasks.task: Check a product idea against real buyer complaints

items.when: When the idea is loose and you want the complaints that sell and a score for the gap
When you have rival product reviews and need complaints ranked with real quotes
When rival products must be set beside the idea on price, features and gaps
Before paying for tooling, to test demand with a pre-order or page and a clear pass mark
When the design suits the maker and you must ask how a real person will hold and use it

tasks.task: Plan prototypes in stages and what each must prove

items.when: When looks-like, works-like and pre-production samples each need a purpose and a test
Before building anything, to rank which unknowns each prototype must settle first
When a rough mock-up could be tested with real users in a week before any costly sample
When people will handle the prototype and you need tasks, notes and a findings summary
Before a test session, to find blockers and word the tasks neutrally
When a prototype fails, to study the actual failure before planning the next test

tasks.task: Brief the look of the product and make concept images

items.when: When the product and brand direction need one visual sheet plan and image prompts
Before settling a look, to see three clearly different directions with one chosen
When the client needs to see the idea as pictures, or a variant of an existing photo
When concept images need sharpening or trying across several image models
When there are two to four directions, to have a fresh reviewer pick one and say what to borrow

tasks.task: Write a garment tech pack a factory can quote from

items.when: When a garment needs callouts, points of measure, tolerances, materials and construction
When you start from product photos and ideas and need exact measures written out
Before sending, to read the pack as the factory and list every place they would have to guess

tasks.task: Build a bill of materials with parts, trims and labels

items.when: When a garment's fabrics, trims, labels and packaging must be listed with placement
When you have a product and a quote and need a cost sheet by part with each maker
When the product has electronics, to find parts that could stall the build and second sources

tasks.task: Run design-for-manufacture questions before quoting

items.when: When the design is close to final and costly or hard-to-make features must be caught
When the design looks done, to list the ways it could fail in making or in use
When the cost target is missed, to question each costly step and try a cheaper way

tasks.task: Choose materials and check sourcing claims

items.when: When suppliers' ethics and environment claims need a questionnaire and a gap list
Before a material claim goes in the spec, to tie it to a test report or supplier document
When the cheaper material wins by default and nobody has asked how long the product will last

tasks.task: Shortlist and vet manufacturers

items.when: When you need a supplier list, scoring rules and negotiation levers before contacting anyone
When factories have answered and each must be scored, with red flags and a pick
When buying from Chinese factories and you need supplier checks, total cost and an order split
When the product is made or packed by a co-packer and the deal must be managed

tasks.task: Build a request-for-quote pack for manufacturers

items.when: When the spec is ready and factories need quantities, packaging, delivery term and questions
When buyer complaints should shape the request and it must be written in maker terms
Before sharing drawings, to get a draft confidentiality agreement for a lawyer to check
Before sending, to read the pack as a factory sales rep and list what they cannot price

tasks.task: Compare factory quotes on the same basis

items.when: When quotes come back and must be laid side by side with gaps listed
When quotes differ in units, currency and delivery terms and need one basis
When you need one quick table, the cash each quote needs and a go or walk call
When deposits are large and each supplier needs a deposit-safety score and terms check

tasks.task: Work out cost per unit at three order sizes

items.when: When quotes have different minimums, tooling and terms and need one cost basis
When freight must be added to get cost per sellable unit and margin
When duty depends on a tariff code and you need the code options and the papers
When price breaks tempt a bigger order and holding cost must be weighed
When the product will sell through retailers, to test margin after their cut and promos
Before the cost sheet goes to the client, to find broken formulas and wrong totals

tasks.task: Prepare to negotiate price breaks, minimums and terms

items.when: When you have the parts list and volume plan and need asks, give-backs and a fallback
When the deposit strains cash and you need terms to ask for
Before the call, to get opening lines, questions and what to listen for

tasks.task: Review a factory sample and write clear comments

items.when: When a sample arrives and you need the steps from measuring to approve or reject
When a sample does not match the spec and the factory needs measurable comments
When each line of the tech pack needs a pass or fail against the sample
When samples come in rounds and you want go or hold each time, with a stop at three
When a fault repeats, to look at the real part in hand before blaming the factory

tasks.task: Prepare safety and labelling questions for a test lab

items.when: When a lab or adviser must decide which US, UK and EU rules apply to this product
When the product crosses borders and you need the rules that apply and who owns each
Before the list goes to the lab, to tie each rule you name to a dated official source

tasks.task: Plan the timeline to the first batch

items.when: When you know what is being made and by whom and need dates for samples, lab and shipping
When a launch date is fixed and every step from samples to warehouse needs an owner
When choosing between a small pilot run and a full first order, to compare both with money and dates
Before promising a date, to imagine the batch arrived late and find why

tasks.task: Ask a supplier for a status, date or document

items.when: When you need a status, a date, a missing answer or a document from a current supplier
When a delay has made you angry and the email must still make them want to help
Before sending to a reader whose first language is not English, to cut idioms and long sentences

tasks.task: Brief a pre-shipment inspection and handle defects

items.when: Before the balance is paid, to give the inspector a brief, a pass rule and release terms
When defect data exists and you need the biggest causes ranked and a plan to cut them
When the factory replies to a defect report and its fix must be tested against your evidence
When corrective actions come in over several rounds and each needs checking against the standard
When the same defect returns, to ask why five times before adding another inspection

tasks.task: Place the first order and get it shipped

items.when: When you want the whole run from tech pack and vetted factory to inspected shipment in order
When forwarders quote differently and every charge must be counted on the same shipment
When customs will ask for papers and you need the list for this route

tasks.task: Decide what to protect before sharing the design

items.when: When the client is unsure what to keep secret, license or share openly
When a factory or designer will see drawings and a confidentiality draft is needed
When the factory sends its own NDA and you need the odd clauses flagged

tasks.task: Write the packaging brief for a designer

items.when: When the product is nearly final and a designer needs materials, sizes and the unboxing
When the pack could do more, to try sense cues with their costs before fixing the brief
Before the brief goes out, to list the marks and warnings the pack may have to carry

always.when: At the start of any sizeable job, to capture the real product, its buyer and its cost target
Whenever the work states a rule, a test standard or a supplier fact, to give it a dated source
Before any document goes to a factory, to read it as they would and find what they must guess

helpers.when: When the product needs a pack designed, with dielines and print-ready files
When supplier terms, contracts and purchase orders need a buyer's eye
When order sizes, lead times and stock cover need planning beyond the first batch
When the batch needs freight booked, customs papers and delivery to a warehouse
When cost of goods is known and the selling price and margin must be set
When safety, marking or import rules need a control check before launch

gaps: No library item writes requirements for a physical product with a target and test method per line; the requirements items are for software
No library item plans staged prototypes for physical goods; the prototype items are for screens and apps
No library item writes an industrial design brief or makes flat sketches and drawings with callouts
No library item builds a size chart and grading table, or a print and embroidery placement spec
No library item checks a design for manufacture by process, such as moulding, sheet metal or cut-and-sew, or sets tolerances
No library item helps choose materials, such as fabrics or plastics, against cost and use
No library item lists product safety and marking rules by region or briefs a test lab beyond the kit skill
No library item writes product instructions, a care label or warning text
No library item covers first steps for a patent or design registration
No library item keeps a spec change log so the factory always works from the latest version
No library item checks a manufacturing agreement or purchase order terms
No library item makes different versions of a tech pack layout or a supplier email to choose between
The library has no tool guide for CAD or tech pack software
